# TrossenRobotics SO-ARM100 (6-DOF, Feetech servos)

<p class="sr-chips"><span class="sr-chip sr-chip-family" data-family="arm">Arms</span><span class="sr-chip">6 joints</span><span class="sr-chip sr-chip-sim">sim</span><span class="sr-chip sr-chip-real">real</span><span class="sr-chip sr-chip-driver">driver: lerobot, strands</span></p>

You have `so100` in a MuJoCo world after one line, and the same object on the hardware with `mode="real"`.

<robot-viewer name="so100"></robot-viewer>

```python
from strands_robots import Robot

robot = Robot("so100")
```

Real hardware, one line per driver that builds it (needs the robot on the wire):

```python title="sketch"
robot = Robot("so100", mode="real", port="/dev/ttyACM0")  # lerobot so100_follower
robot = Robot("so100", mode="real", driver="strands", port="/dev/ttyACM0")  # FeetechDriver
```

Aliases `Robot()` accepts: `so100_4cam`, `so100_dualcam`, `so100_follower`, `so_arm100`, `trs_so_arm100`.

| Model joint | Action key |
|---|---|
| `Rotation` | `shoulder_pan` |
| `Pitch` | `shoulder_lift` |
| `Elbow` | `elbow_flex` |
| `Wrist_Pitch` | `wrist_flex` |
| `Wrist_Roll` | `wrist_roll` |
| `Jaw` | `gripper` |

Gripper actuator `Jaw`: closed at the low end of travel, open at the high end.

## Hardware

**lerobot.** `Robot("so100", mode="real")` builds lerobot's `so100_follower` with `pip install 'strands-robots[lerobot]'`; `port=` is the serial device and `cameras=` the lerobot camera dict. This is the default when `driver=` is not given.

**`FeetechDriver`** (selected with `driver="strands"`) speaks Feetech STS/SMS serial bus. Source: `strands_robots/drivers/feetech/driver.py`.

| | |
|---|---|
| `port=` | serial device of the SCS bus, for example `"/dev/ttyACM0"` or `"/dev/tty.usbserial-*"` |
| SDK | `pyserial` (`pip install pyserial`); calibration file from `lerobot-calibrate` |
| Other kwargs | `baud_rate=1_000_000`, `calibration=<path or records>`, `motor_ids=()`, `timeout=1.0`, `transport="serial"` or `"twin"` |
| Action keys | degrees per joint, `gripper` in percent open; keys `shoulder_pan` or `shoulder_pan.pos` |

What the driver checks before it writes:

- the bus opens the port and discovers the servo ids on connect
- without `calibration=` the driver reads and commands the servo's full travel, not the arm's measured travel; `get_status` reports `calibration_source`
- `stop` releases torque on every motor and names any that stayed driven
- `transport="twin"` answers the same verbs from the arm's MuJoCo model
